geometric_derivation.claim: concavity-compression stability ratio (max sustainable tangential/compressive force before the head rolls over the glenoid rim) = tan(theta_max), where theta_max is the half-angle subtended by the glenoid concavity's rim at its own center of curvature -- a frictionless rigid-body contact-equilibrium identity (2-force-member equilibrium forces the applied resultant's angle-from-axis to equal the current contact-normal angle; the LIMIT is reached exactly when that angle equals the rim's own subtended half-angle), NOT a curve-fit.
geometric_derivation.depth_to_angle_relation: cos(theta_max) = 1 - depth/R_g  (R_g = concavity's own radius of curvature; standard spherical-cap sagitta relation)
qualitative_predictions_matching_literat: ratio increases monotonically with depth -- matches Lippitt 1993's own observation that stability is 'greatest magnitude superiorly and inferiorly... attributed to greater glenoid depth in these directions'

ratio should be approximately LOAD-INDEPENDENT (pure function of geometry, not of the compressive-force magnitude) -- consistent with (though not explicitly broken out as a same-vs-different number in) Lippitt 1993's report of one consistent 'up to 60%' figure across both the 50N and 100N test conditions

removing/detaching the labrum reduces effective depth, hence reduces theta_max, hence reduces the ratio -- matches both papers' qualitative direction (Lippitt: resection reduced effectiveness ~20%; Howell: Bankart-type detachment nearly halves AP depth)

step_1_calibrate_Rg_from_SI_direction_on.caveat: R_g is BACK-SOLVED (implied), not an independently-measured glenoid radius-of-curvature from a third source -- this session did not live-verify a separate glenoid/humeral radius-of-curvature paper

step_2_predict_AP_direction_using_ONLY_t.assessment: order-of-magnitude consistent (predicted 32.9% AP-specific reduction vs. Lippitt's independently-reported ~20% ALL-directions-averaged reduction after full labral excision) -- a genuine cross-paper check (neither paper's number was used to fit the other), NOT an exact-match claim: different lesion scope (AP-only Bankart-type vs full circumferential excision) and different directions, so exact numeric equality is not expected or claimed.

falsifier_verdict.part_a_concavity_compression_ratio_vs_de: PASS (external anchor + geometric derivation) -- Lippitt 1993's ratio (0.60, labrum intact) and Howell 1989's depth (9mm SI) are jointly consistent under a single back-solved R_g via a frictionless contact-geometry identity derived this session; that SAME R_g, applied out-of-sample to Howell's independently-measured AP depths, predicts a stability-ratio reduction after labral detachment in the same order of magnitude as Lippitt's own independently-reported reduction. Not a from-scratch finite-element re-derivation of the cadaveric experiment (out of this session's scope -- no contact-mechanics substrate exists in this repo, checked), but a genuine, non-tautological, cross-paper over-determination.
falsifier_verdict.part_b_deltoid_cuff_coronal_couple_cente: PASS, but ONLY on the anatomically-valid (donor) substrate, machine-measured this session -- deltoid-alone ratio=3.25 (unstable, large +superior shear); deltoid+cuff ratio=1.01 (3.2x improvement), monotonic across all 4 deltoid-activation levels x 5 cuff-activation levels (20/20 grid points). The SAME test on the twin (subject2) model FAILS at all 4 poses -- but this negative was FORCED through OODA to its root cause (11/11 muscle origins mis-parented to torso, not scapula_r, a pre-existing, already-partially-disclosed model-fidelity gap) rather than accepted as a refutation of the mechanism. This is a diagnosed MODEL-FIDELITY gap in subject2's own twin, not a falsification of concavity-compression/force-couple stability.
falsifier_verdict.deltoid_alone_adversary_required_to_FAIL: CONFIRMED FAILED (in the required direction) on the donor substrate: ratio 3.25 is the WORST point in the entire 20-point grid; every unit of added cuff activation, at every deltoid activation level, strictly improves it.
